title: Astronomers Find Potentially Habitable Planets, Just 40 Light Years Away
main_content:
So far we are still alone in the universe, but little by little, astronomers around the world are expanding our celestial neighborhood. They just announced three new candidates that could potentially support life.

And they’re only 40 light years away, in the constellation Aquarius.

The three planets are orbiting what is called an ultra-cool dwarf star and have temperatures well below the 400 Kelvin range (about 120 Celsius) that is considered cool enough to support life. The reason it has taken so long to find these close-by planets is because dwarf stars are invisible to optical telescopes.

questions.question: What suggests that the three planets could potentially support life?
options: Their orbit around an ultra-cool dwarf star
Their temperatures are well below the 400 Kelvin range
Their location in the constellation Aquarius
questions.answer: Their temperatures are well below the 400 Kelvin range

questions.question: Why is it hard to find planets like these?
options: They are located in the constellation Aquarius
Their low temperatures make them difficult to observe
Dwarf stars are invisible to optical telescopes
They are only visible from Earth at night
questions.answer: Dwarf stars are invisible to optical telescopes
